topics.topic: Filesystem paths accessible to sandboxed function code
questions: May agent code read or write arbitrary paths inside the exchange directory and read arbitrary runtime files, or may it access only runner-provided input artifacts?
May agent code itself read and write arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or is that directory accessible only to the runner for transporting inputs and outputs?
May agent code open and read arbitrary files in the read-only runtime, or may it access only its supplied inputs and required imports?

judgement.why: This is the same sandbox-filesystem-access question already judged, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Filesystem access available to sandboxed function code
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Permitted api_base_url forms and deterministic joining with operation paths
questions: Are base URLs containing a path, query, fragment, user information, unusual authority spelling, or multiple trailing slashes valid, and exactly how are they joined to the operation path?
Which exact api_base_url forms are valid, and how are its authority and optional path combined with the operation path without parser-dependent normalization?
May api_base_url contain user information, a query, a fragment, or a non-root path, and are one or all trailing slashes removed before joining?

judgement.why: This is the same base-URL grammar and joining question already assigned to a later state.

precedent.topic: Allowed base-URL components and exact joining and normalization rules
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Validation, duplicate-key handling, and failure ordering for malformed manifest records
questions: How are structurally malformed but valid-JSON manifest records handled—for example a non-string `service`, non-list `capabilities`, non-object capability, missing or non-string capability `name`, duplicate JSON keys, or facts JCS cannot canonicalize?
Which manifest field shapes are valid, in what check order are malformed shapes refused, and which refusal detail applies to each malformed nested value?
Are duplicate object member names anywhere in a manifest record refused, and under which manifest-mismatch check?

judgement.why: This is the same manifest-schema and malformed-field-ordering question already judged.

precedent.topic: Accepted manifest schema and malformed-field error precedence
precedent.why: Exact manifest shapes, field types and malformed-field ordering are schema and contract details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Which concluded node-attempt outcomes permit retrying an element
questions: Does a `service_unreachable` or resolved-`not_applied` NodeExecution count as a concluded record that blocks the element, or only as a concluded attempt that permits a later attempt?
Which concluded NodeExecution statuses permit the element to be attempted again, and how does that exception interact with the rule that concluded elements never execute again?
Is a service_unreachable NodeExecution a concluded element or only a concluded attempt, and what explicit exception permits the next attempt?

quotes: a concluded element is never executed again

Resume, by the owner or an agent, sends again, in (`node_id`, `map_index`)
   order — an element without `map_index` before index 0 — every element waiting
   on `service_unreachable`.
judgement.why: One rule forbids executing a concluded element again while another requires reaching and sending the same waiting element again.

topics.topic: Accepted media-type grammar and canonicalization for file ports
questions: What media-type grammar is accepted for file ports, is case canonicalized, and are parameters permitted in the declared value?
What syntax must a port media_type satisfy before it can be placed in an HTTP header, and are parameters or control characters allowed?

judgement.why: This is the same media-type syntax, parsing and comparison question already assigned to a later state.

precedent.topic: Media-type syntax, parsing, and response matching
precedent.why: Media-type grammar, parsing, header validity and serialization are format and field-constraint decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Atomicity and recovery of admission-verdict recording with automatic activation
questions: Must recording the admitted verdict and its automatic activation be one atomic store transaction, or may a crash leave an admitted verdict recorded without its activation until the implementation is submitted again?
If the kernel crashes or a store call fails after recording an admitted verdict but before recording its activation, what state and response are required, and is activation recovered automatically?

quotes:
Each is one transaction (K-17); the module named is its only caller. Records
not listed are never written.
| `record_admission_verdict` | `functions` | AdmissionVerdict M08, and Activation M09 when admitted and not current |
judgement.why: The later store contract makes the verdict and automatic activation writes one atomic transaction.

topics.topic: Canonical ordering of duplicate-looking flow edges and constants for hashing and failure selection
questions: How are two different edges with identical endpoint tuples, or two different constants targeting the same port, ordered for hashing and first-failure selection?
How are two different constants with the same destination ordered for identity hashing and for selecting the first proof failure?
How are otherwise identical-endpoint edges with different guards ordered for flow identity and first-failure selection?

judgement.why: This is the same missing tie-breaker question for flow hashing and proof ordering already judged.

precedent.topic: Canonical ordering of duplicate or tied FlowVersion components before hashing
quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
precedent.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Classification of malformed HTTP responses and invalid response Content-Type headers
questions: Which HTTP syntax and duplicate-header cases count as malformed, so that different HTTP client libraries cannot classify the same response differently?
What happens when Content-Type is syntactically invalid but contains text from which a type and subtype could be extracted?

judgement.why: Exact HTTP syntax, header parsing and Content-Type validity are transport-format and encoding rules belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Credential and required-header decoding, wire encoding, character rules, and size limits
questions: Exactly how is a credential file decoded and stripped, which Unicode or ASCII characters are forbidden, how is the resulting value encoded on the HTTP wire, and what maximum size is accepted?
What maximum size applies to credential and required-header names and values, and what refusal occurs when it is exceeded?

judgement.why: Credential stripping, character sets, wire encoding and field-size constraints are encoding, format and field-contract details belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Definition and enforcement of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: Is loopback determined from an IP literal in the URL, from DNS resolution, or from the actual connected peer address, and how are DNS changes or multiple resolved addresses handled?
What counts as a loopback host, and must DNS resolution be pinned and checked so a hostname cannot resolve differently between validation and connection?

judgement.why: This is the same definition and enforcement question for the plain-HTTP loopback exception already judged.

precedent.topic: Definition and evaluation of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Encoding or rejection of multipart names and filenames
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text and CR/LF in a port name represented or refused when used in multipart headers?
Which port names are valid in quoted multipart parameters, and how are quotes, backslashes, control characters and non-ASCII characters escaped or refused?

judgement.why: This is the same multipart parameter escaping and port-name validity question already assigned to a later state.

precedent.topic: Encoding or rejection of unsafe multipart port names
precedent.why: Multipart header escaping, media-type grammar, boundary generation and wire framing are format and encoding decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Environmental observations that must be hidden or fixed for deterministic function execution
questions: How is determinism guaranteed when permitted Python can observe varying facts such as object identities, process/runtime details, or other standard-library state not trapped by A03?
Which observable standard-library or operating-system facts, beyond clocks and named randomness APIs, must be hidden or fixed so that equal inputs are guaranteed to produce equal outputs?

judgement.why: This is the same question about untrapped environmental nondeterminism in sandbox execution already judged.

precedent.topic: Handling of untrapped nondeterminism in sandboxed execution
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Exact equality semantics for guard values
questions: What exact equality rule is used for guard values, including numeric forms such as `1` and `1.0` and structured enum values?
Is guard equality JSON Schema equality, equality of canonical JSON bytes, or host-language equality, especially for numbers such as 1 and 1.0 and for booleans versus numbers?

judgement.why: This is the same JSON guard-value equality question already answered by later text.

precedent.topic: Equality semantics for JSON guard values
quotes: advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
precedent.why: The later run contract defines guard equality as equality of canonical JSON text.

topics.topic: Observable approval result when a pre-send recheck prevents sending
questions: What is the promised result of approving a requested effect when the rebuilt request changed or a pre-send check now fails: must the approved request run, may approval merely leave the run waiting, or may a different request run under a grant?
What observable result must the approve action return when the decision is recorded but the effect cannot be sent because a pre-send check now fails?

quotes: the effect runs on the exact input shown

The approval itself always succeeds; when a pre-send check then
   fails (A09 rule 6), nothing is sent, the element concludes `operation_failed`
   and the approval stays `approved` and unused, void once the run ends.
judgement.why: State 0 promises that approval runs the shown effect, while A10 permits a successful approval that sends nothing and instead fails the element.

topics.topic: Representation and disclosure class of many-file outputs, including empty lists
questions: What class does an empty output list of a mapped operation node receive when the binding's output class differs from the highest input class?
Where is the class and ordered-list identity of a delivered many-file value represented, especially when individual files may have different recorded classes?
How does a NodeExecution encode an empty many-file output and its class when there is no SpooledFile reference on which to carry either fact?

quotes: advance_run: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A value port's PortRef names exactly one StoredValue; a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's value_schema as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change; when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is; only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing; a mapped node's file output is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, derived from the elements' NodeExecutions whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, since no record of its own holds it, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input; a mapped element receives the list element at its map_index as its own StoredValue of the map_over port's value_schema and the list's class, or the spooled file at that position.
judgement.why: The later run contract represents a many-file output as an ordered SpooledFilesRef with its own disclosure class and explicitly assigns an empty list the highest class among the node's inputs.

topics.topic: Required completeness of authored TrialCase inputs and expected outputs
questions: Must inputs contain exactly every input port and no extras, and when expected outputs are present must they contain exactly every output port, or may either set be partial?
Must authored trial inputs contain exactly every input port and no unknown ports, and in what order are missing and extra ports refused?
When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly all output ports, or may it assert only a subset?

judgement.why: This is the same required and optional TrialCase port-set question already assigned to State 6 schemas.

precedent.topic: Required and permitted trial-case input and expected-output fields
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Resource bounds and over-limit outcomes for manifests and other host-controlled inputs
questions: What happens when one of these host-controlled files or collections is arbitrarily large?
What bounds apply while reading and parsing untrusted manifest data, and is an over-limit record a manifest mismatch or a start failure?

judgement.why: This is the same ceiling question for manifest and other host-controlled material already answered by later text.

precedent.topic: Size ceilings for externally supplied and outbound request material
quotes:
The manifest, like the installation file, is the
   owner's trusted input at a revision the owner chose: the release's closed
   list of ceilings (A20 rule 1) has none for it, and none for the headers or
   capabilities it declares. What reaches a service or an agent stays bounded
   where it is used — a request's input values by `stored_value_bytes_max`, a
   response by `service_response_bytes_max`, a refusal's reason by
   `bounded_text_bytes_max`; a record too large to read is one that cannot be
   read (State 5, closed question 8).
precedent.why: The State 6 text explicitly assigns no ceiling to trusted manifest material, headers or capabilities and identifies the per-use bounds that apply to request inputs, responses and reasons.

topics.topic: Atomic withholding and measurement order for oversized mapped outputs
questions: When a mapped node has several used outputs and only one collected list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, are all outputs withheld atomically, can smaller outputs still reach flow outputs or dependants, and in what port order are lists measured?

topics.topic: Atomicity of compound creation and publication actions
questions: For each compound action, may a crash leave a slot without its first contract, a flow without its first version, or published bytes without the intended record, or must each logical action be atomic?

topics.topic: Attempt-number association when approval resumes a not-sent request
questions: When that approval requested for attempt 1 authorizes the resumed send recorded as attempt 2, does its attempt_number remain 1, change to 2, or is reuse across attempt numbers forbidden?

topics.topic: Bounding and handling sandbox stdout and stderr
questions: Where do stdout and stderr go, how are their bytes bounded, and what outcome results if code writes indefinitely to them?

topics.topic: Canonical JSON structure hashed for idempotency keys
questions: Is the hashed JSON an object keyed by field name, a list in manifest order, or another structure?

topics.topic: Configuration token-list reread, retry, and digest-caching state machine
questions: What exact read/retry and cached-digest state machine runs before each request when the configuration changes or cannot be read?

topics.topic: Evidence and precedence used to classify sandbox resource exhaustion
questions: What observable evidence classifies memory, process-count or scratch exhaustion as resource_exhausted rather than crashed or a caught user exception?

topics.topic: Exact filesystem ownership and permission requirements for private data storage
questions: What exact ownership and permission checks define “private,” including permissions on parent directories, the SQLite files, temporary files and spool subdirectories?

topics.topic: Failure ordering among invalid or duplicated required manifest headers
questions: When several required headers are duplicated or invalid, what order selects the first reported header if the manifest representation does not provide a normative order?

topics.topic: Handling content-addressed filename collisions with mismatching bytes or size
questions: If a file already exists under the expected digest but its bytes or size differ, does the store fail, stop the kernel, or reuse it solely by name?

topics.topic: Handling oversized value outputs from trial executions
questions: What happens when a trial execution returns a schema-valid value larger than `stored_value_bytes_max` but within its contract's `output_bytes` bound, since a trial execution is not a flow node?

topics.topic: How a run identifies a specific activation occurrence
questions: How does a run identify the exact FlowActivation when the same flow version can be deactivated and activated again multiple times?

topics.topic: How manifest files are read at a repository revision
questions: How is a file read “at” a revision: from a checked-out directory, through a repository object lookup, or by requiring the working tree to equal that revision, and what happens for an invalid or unavailable revision?

topics.topic: Lifetime uniqueness and reuse rules for actor names
questions: May a removed agent name later be assigned to a different token or agent, thereby making old and new actions indistinguishable, or must names be permanently unique for the installation's lifetime?

topics.topic: Multipart boundary selection and body-collision handling
questions: How is a boundary selected, and what happens if the selected boundary byte sequence occurs in a part body?

topics.topic: OperationBinding validation behavior when port names are duplicated
questions: How are key-field and request-shape checks evaluated when duplicate port names exist, given that uniqueness is checked later and the earlier checks may select different duplicate declarations?

topics.topic: Ordering of multiple records written in one transaction
questions: How are multiple records written by one transaction ordered for activation identity, pagination, oldest-first processing and all other uses of store position?

topics.topic: Recorded outcome when sandbox cleanup cannot be confirmed after failure
questions: If an execution first times out or exhausts a resource and cleanup then cannot be confirmed, which outcome is recorded?

topics.topic: Redaction policy for payload-bearing function exception details
questions: If an exception message contains an input value or other payload, is that text stored verbatim, redacted, or replaced with a fixed diagnostic?

topics.topic: Required HTTP protocol version and connection behavior
questions: Which HTTP protocol version and connection behavior must the invoker use so that the required wire headers and sent/not-sent boundary have one implementation-independent meaning?

topics.topic: Retention or deletion policy for unreferenced content-addressed value files
questions: Are unreferenced content-addressed value files retained forever, or must they be removed so trial fixtures are the only files kept beyond a run?

topics.topic: Timestamp semantics for NodeExecutions that do not execute code
questions: What events supply `started_at` and `ended_at` for owner refusal, guard skip, upstream failure, receiving-side validation failure and an empty mapped node?

topics.topic: Whether NodeExecution identity is issued or content-substitutable
questions: Is a NodeExecution a content-substitutable value, or an issued entity identified by run, node, element and attempt number?

topics.topic: Whether deterministic pseudorandom generation is allowed
questions: Is deterministic pseudorandom generation part of the allowed function language despite the absolute State 0 prohibition?

topics.topic: Whether empty FlowNode identifiers are permitted
questions: May a FlowNode have an empty node_id, which would collide with the endpoint sentinel?

topics.topic: Whether file-carriage ports may be used as guards
questions: Must a guard port have `value` carriage, or may a `file` output whose schema appears closed be used as a guard?

topics.topic: Whether functions may synthesize new files inside a flow
questions: May a function synthesize a new file from value inputs, or must every file in a run originate as an operation-node output?

topics.topic: Whether invalid or unloadable Python creates an Implementation
questions: Does syntactically invalid or unloadable Python create an Implementation and undergo admission, or is the authoring request refused without creating it?

topics.topic: Whether releasing a failed run requires confirmed physical file deletion
questions: Does a release succeed when files remain physically present, and does "released" mean logical inaccessibility or confirmed deletion?

topics.topic: Whether transformed or encoded credentials are covered by secret non-disclosure
questions: May an encoded or transformed service credential be stored and returned when the binding class permits it, or must the no-secret guarantee cover recognizable encodings and transformations too?

topics.topic: Which prior implementations are eligible for rollback
questions: Does “earlier implementation” mean any previously submitted implementation, or only one that was previously active?

topics.topic: Which standard-library clock sources are prohibited
questions: Are unlisted standard-library clock sources such as `time.clock_gettime`, `os.times` and `resource.getrusage` allowed, or must the no-clock rule also block them?
